---
sidebar: physical-ai
title: "Physical AI"
subtitle: "Machine Learning Systems That Sense and Act"
---

Physical AI systems sense their surroundings and act on them. In this course,
students build and evaluate a robot whose learned policy proposes actions and
whose independent governor decides whether to permit them. Measurements of the
resulting motion inform the next decision.
The course draws on [MLSysBook Volume IV](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol4/) and its
[Physical AI lab sequence](eth-spring-2027/index.qmd#labs).

## Course offerings

[**ETH Zurich · Spring 2027**](eth-spring-2027/index.qmd) — draft course plan for a
project seminar and hardware studio taught by Vijay Janapa Reddi, with teaching
assistant Andrea Mattia Garavagno. The offering page contains the course overview,
syllabus, schedule, and links to the labs.

## For instructors {#for-instructors}

The [Physical AI instructor guide](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/vol4/)
covers teaching format, student background, station and compute requirements,
qualification, and assessment. The ETH offering provides a draft plan that other
institutions can adapt; its equipment and deployment path still require staff
qualification.

## Earlier related courses {#earlier-related-courses}

[**Autonomous Machines · Harvard CS249r · Fall 2019**](https://brianplancher.com/courses/cs249r_autonomous/)
examined hardware and software for autonomous vehicles, drones, ground robots,
and manipulators. Its [syllabus](https://brianplancher.com/files/CS249_F19_Syllabus.pdf),
[research paper list](https://brianplancher.com/files/CS249_F19_Papers.pdf), and
[introductory lecture slides](https://brianplancher.com/files/CS249_F19_IntroSlides.pdf)
remain available as related teaching resources. This offering predates the
current textbook and is preserved under its original title.

The [course directory](../index.qmd) lists other learning paths and courses at
other institutions that use MLSysBook.
